---
title: "USER-GUIDE-v001"
subtitle: "How to make, set up and update AI-assisted projects with yrAiProject"
---

## What this repository is for {#sec-purpose}

Every project for AI-assisted work gets the same base, so that people and AI agents find the same things in the
same places:

- `AGENTS.md`: the rules for every AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and others) and every
  collaborator. It holds the project's rules and a copy of the **shared rules**, which apply to every project.
- `CLAUDE.md`: the import line `@AGENTS.md`, so that Claude Code reads the same rules.
- **Pending work**: a list of things to do later, kept as GitHub issues. Claude Code shows how many are open when a
  session starts (@sec-pending).
- `docs/`: the **project-docs Quarto book**: the SPECs, the guides and the plans, with the
  `new-doc` skill that adds a document (@sec-new-doc).
- `.yrAiProject/manifest.json`: the record of the template version and the parts that the project has.

One command does everything: **`yrAiProject.sh`**.

```bash
yrAiProject.sh new PATH          # make a new project
yrAiProject.sh status [PATH]     # what state is this project in? (changes nothing)
yrAiProject.sh update [PATH]     # set up an existing project, or bring it up to date
yrAiProject.sh list              # the template versions
yrAiProject.sh --help            # every command and option
```

`PATH` is the project folder. For `status` and `update`, the default is the git repository that you are in.

## Set up a computer {#sec-setup}

You need Dropbox (synced), Python 3.8 or later, git and Quarto. For pending work and `--github`, you also need the
`gh` command, logged in (`gh auth login`). This works on Linux, and in Git Bash on Windows.

1. Make sure that the Dropbox tools folder is on `PATH`. The tools folder holds `yrAiProject.sh`. On Linux,
   `~/.bashrc` has the line `export PATH="$PATH:$HOME/Dropbox/tools"`.
2. Run once (safe to run again):

   ```bash
   ~/Dropbox/tools/yrAiProject.sh setup-computer
   ```

   It checks the `PATH`, and it adds an import line to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Then Claude Code follows the shared
   rules in every project on this computer. `setup-computer --check` only reports.
3. Test: `yrAiProject.sh list` shows the template versions.

On Windows, `python3` can be a Microsoft Store placeholder that does not run. `yrAiProject.sh` then uses `python`
or `py -3`.

## It asks before it changes anything {#sec-confirm}

`new` and `update` first show what they would do:

- `+ add` a file that they would add;
- `~ change` a file that they would change, with the changes line by line (lines that start with `+` would be
  added, lines that start with `-` would be removed);
- `= keep` a file that they leave alone, and why.

Then they ask `Apply these changes? [y/N]`. Answer `y` to apply; anything else changes nothing.

| You want to | Add |
|---|---|
| Only see the plan, and change nothing | `--dry-run` |
| Apply without the question (in a script) | `-y` |

With no terminal to ask in (a script, or an AI agent such as Claude Code) and no `-y`, the tool shows the plan,
changes nothing, and stops with exit status 6. An AI agent should run `--dry-run`, show you the plan, and use `-y`
only after you say yes.

## Make a project {#sec-make}

```bash
yrAiProject.sh new --title "Photo Checks" --description "Reads photos of checks into a spreadsheet." ~/Dropbox/_yrAiCoding/yrPhotoChecks
yrAiProject.sh new --type book --title "Python for Beginners" ~/Dropbox/_yrQuarto-master/yrPythonBook
```

The folder must not exist, or must be empty, or must hold only `.git`. Its name is the project name. After you
confirm, the tool:

1. copies the shared template files, then the files of the type, and fills in the project name, title,
   description, type, date and template version;
2. copies the shared rules into `AGENTS.md`;
3. writes the record, `.yrAiProject/manifest.json`;
4. makes a git repository (branch `main`) and commits the files;
5. with `--github`: makes a private GitHub repository with the folder name, pushes, and makes the labels for
   pending work.

Then:

1. In `README.md`, write the "Getting started" section.
2. In `docs/SPEC-v0.1.0.qmd`, write what the first version must do.
3. Look at the books: `quarto preview docs` (and `quarto preview` in a book project).

| Type | Use it for | What it adds to the shared files |
|---|---|---|
| `work` (the default) | Any work: programs, data, research, ... | A README for any kind of work |
| `book` | A Quarto book that you publish | The main book at the root (`_quarto.yml`, `index.qmd`, `intro.qmd`), a README for a book, and `docs/PLANNING-v001.qmd` for the plans for the main book |

## See the state of a project {#sec-status}

```bash
yrAiProject.sh status ~/Dropbox/_yrQuarto-master/yrThinkPython
```

```
/home/yitz/Dropbox/_yrQuarto-master/yrThinkPython
  partly set up: it has rules, but no record of a version (set up by hand, or with the old agents-init tool)
  rules         out of date: update would change 1 file(s)
  pending-work  not installed: update adds it (3 file(s))
  docs          not installed (optional: update --with-docs)
```

The first line says whether the project was **never set up**, is **partly set up** (it has some parts, but no
record), was set up with an **older version**, or is **up to date**. Then there is one line for each part. Files
that you changed by hand are counted too: `update` leaves them alone. `status` changes nothing.

## Set up an existing project, or update one {#sec-update}

```bash
yrAiProject.sh update --dry-run      # first look (in the project folder)
yrAiProject.sh update                # then do it: it shows the plan again and asks
```

`update` works on any folder: one that was never set up, one that was set up by hand or with the old tools, and one
made by `yrAiProject.sh new`. It adds only the **parts** that a project needs, never the whole template:

| Part | What it is | `update` |
|---|---|---|
| `rules` | The shared rules in `AGENTS.md`, and `@AGENTS.md` in `CLAUDE.md` | always |
| `pending-work` | The pending-work skill, and its hook in `.claude/settings.json` | yes; `--no-pending-work` to skip it (remembered) |
| `docs` | The project-docs Quarto book in `docs/`, and the `new-doc` skill | only with `--with-docs` (then kept up to date) |

What `update` does with the files:

- In `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/settings.json`, it changes only the shared-rules block, the import line
  and the hook. Your own rules and settings stay.
- **Tool files** (the skills in `.claude/skills/`, and the guides in `docs/`) get the newest version, unless you
  changed them by hand: those it leaves alone, and `status` counts them. To take the newest version of such a file,
  delete it (or rename it), then run `update`.
- **Starting files** (the first SPEC, the docs `_quarto.yml`, ...) are added once; then they are
  yours, and `update` never changes them. It never adds a README, `.gitignore` or a main book to an existing
  project.
- It makes no commit. Look at the changes (`git status`, `git diff`), then commit them. If a file that it would
  change has uncommitted changes, it warns you first.

After you change the shared rules, or after a new template version, run `yrAiProject.sh update` in each project.

## Pending work {#sec-pending}

Pending items are things to do later, so that they are not forgotten. You don't use GitHub yourself: tell the agent,
for example "add a pending item: ...", "list pending", "let's work on #12", or "#12 is no longer needed".

- When a Claude Code session starts (and after `/clear`), a hook shows how many items are open, for example
  `Pending work: 12 pending items (3 high, 5 medium, 4 low)`. The list itself is not loaded, because a long list
  uses up the agent's context. Say "list pending" to see it.
- Each item is a GitHub issue in the project's repository with the label `pending-work`, a category label and a
  priority label. `_pending-work/pendingWork.md` is a saved copy, for when GitHub cannot be reached.
- A project with no GitHub repository yet keeps its items in `_pending-work/queue.md` until it has one.
- Once, in a project with a GitHub repository, make the labels:
  `bash .claude/skills/pending-work/scripts/pending.sh setup-labels` (`new --github` does it for you).
- The details: `.claude/skills/pending-work/SKILL.md`, and `bash .claude/skills/pending-work/scripts/pending.sh
  --help`.

## The Quarto books of a project {#sec-books}

Each book is a folder with its own `_quarto.yml`. Give `quarto` the folder of the book:

| Book | Preview | Render | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main book (book projects) | `quarto preview` | `quarto render` | `_book/index.html` |
| Project docs | `quarto preview docs` | `quarto render docs` | `docs/_book/index.html` |

Run the commands from the project folder. Both previews can run at the same time. The QUARTO-GUIDE in each
project tells more.

## Add documents: the new-doc skill {#sec-new-doc}

Ask your AI agent for a new document ("make the next SPEC", "add a USER-GUIDE"), or run the script yourself:

```bash
python3 .claude/skills/new-doc/new_doc.py                       # the next SPEC
python3 .claude/skills/new-doc/new_doc.py USER-GUIDE --title "How to use the tool"
python3 .claude/skills/new-doc/new_doc.py --help                # all the options
```

- **A SPEC is the default type.** A SPEC has the version of its development step: `SPEC-v0.1.0.qmd`, then
  `SPEC-v0.1.1.qmd` (the default next version), or the version that you give with `--version`.
- **Other types:** `USER-GUIDE`, `DESIGN-GUIDE`, `PLANNING`, or any name in capital letters. They have a
  copy number: `USER-GUIDE-v001.qmd`. The next copy, `-v002`, is only for when you want to keep the old copy next
  to the new one.
- A new version starts as a copy of the newest version (use `--blank` for an empty outline).
- The script lists the new file in `docs/_quarto.yml`, above the older versions.

There are no PRD documents: a SPEC holds the requirements. There is no TODO document: work to do later is a
pending item (@sec-pending). The DOC-GUIDE in each project gives all the rules.

## The shared rules for AI agents {#sec-rules}

The shared rules are in `rules/AGENTS.md` of this repository, for example "every script has `--help`". They
reach the agents in two ways:

| Who | How they get the rules |
|---|---|
| Claude Code on your computers | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` imports `rules/AGENTS.md` (`setup-computer` adds the line) |
| Collaborators, any AI agent, cloud agents | A copy in the project's `AGENTS.md`, between `<!-- begin shared rules -->` and `<!-- end shared rules -->` (`new` and `update` put it there) |

To change a shared rule: edit `rules/AGENTS.md`, and commit it. Then, in each project, run `yrAiProject.sh update`
and commit the change. `yrAiProject.sh status` shows which projects have an old copy.

## Options {#sec-options}

| Command and option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `new PATH` | Make a project in `PATH` |
| `  --type work\|book` | The project type (default `work`) |
| `  --title TEXT` | The project title (default: the folder name) |
| `  --description TEXT` | One sentence that says what the project is for (default: a TODO line) |
| `  --version VER` | The template version (default: the newest) |
| `  --github` | Also make a private GitHub repository, push to it, and make the pending-work labels |
| `  --strict-empty` | Refuse a folder that holds anything, even only `.git` |
| `status [PATH]` | Show the state of a project; change nothing |
| `update [PATH]` | Set up, or bring up to date, an existing project |
| `  --with-docs` | Also add the project-docs book and the new-doc skill |
| `  --no-pending-work` | Don't add pending work (remembered) |
| `  --with-pending-work` | Add pending work after an earlier `--no-pending-work` |
| `  --version VER` | The template version (default: the newest) |
| `new` and `update`: `--dry-run` | Show the plan; change nothing |
| `new` and `update`: `-y`, `--yes` | Don't ask |
| `list` | List the template versions and their types |
| `setup-computer [--check]` | Set up this computer (@sec-setup) |
| `-h`, `--help` | Show the help and stop |

Exit status: 0 OK; 1 `status` found something to do, or you answered no; 2 bad options, a missing template or a
missing tool; 3 `new`: the folder is not empty; 5 git or gh failed; 6 the tool needs your answer but there is no
terminal (use `-y` or `--dry-run`).

## Change the templates {#sec-change}

1. A released template version does not change. A version is released when it has the git tag
   `templates-vX.Y.Z`. Projects record their version, and `status` compares it with the newest.
2. To change the templates, copy the newest version folder to a new version, for example `templates/v0.4.0/`, and
   change the copy. `yrAiProject.sh` uses the newest version.
3. Write a SPEC for the new version (`docs/SPEC-v0.4.0.qmd`), and update this guide.
4. Run `python3 tests/selftest.py`. It must print `OK`. Then render this book: `quarto render docs`.
5. Commit, and tag the version: `git tag templates-v0.4.0`.

## Older tools {#sec-retired}

- **yrNewAiProject.sh and agents-init.sh** (template v0.2.0) are replaced by `yrAiProject.sh`. The old names still
  exist in the tools folder, but they only print the new command:

  | Old | New |
  |---|---|
  | `yrNewAiProject.sh PATH` | `yrAiProject.sh new PATH` |
  | `yrNewAiProject.sh --add-to-existing PATH` | `yrAiProject.sh update PATH` |
  | `yrNewAiProject.sh --verify PATH` | `yrAiProject.sh status PATH` |
  | `agents-init.sh [DIR]` | `yrAiProject.sh update [DIR]` |
  | `agents-init.sh --check` / `--diff` | `yrAiProject.sh status` / `update --dry-run` |
  | `bin/setup-computer.sh` | `yrAiProject.sh setup-computer` |

- **No longer supported** (no project uses them): template v0.0.1 (type `generic`), and the records of the
  retired `yraiproject` tool and of `yrNewAiProject` (`.yrAiProjectTemplate/manifest.json`). They are in the git
  history: tag `yraiproject-final` (the pip-installed `yraiproject` tool of version 0.1.0, and v0.0.1) and tag
  `templates-v0.2.0` (`yrNewAiProject`).
